linux_environment.os: Ubuntu 26.04.1 in a private root filesystem on WSL2
linux_environment.network: Private network namespace, slirp4netns/libslirp NAT, tap0 MTU 1500
linux_environment.impairment: tc netem on namespace egress; affects publisher and browser traffic only
linux_environment.publisher: Original extracted Linux release binaries; no transport instrumentation

initial_setup_failures.cause: Missing libsrt1.5-openssl prevented FFmpeg plugin loading; installed and reran
Missing libmbedtls21/libmbedx509-7 prevented preview core outputs plugin loading; installed and reran
Candidate-rewriting proxy never established ICE; discarded that injector and used private-namespace netem; no production code changes

limitations: Fresh Mac release signing/notarization/stapling/Gatekeeper checks ran in CI; no fresh native Mac playback of this media-clock/pacing revision.
Linux tests used software rendering and x264 under WSL2; no Linux hardware-encoder, physical device, or Browser Source certification.
Network loss and the deliberate outage produced freezes, especially on TURN/TLS; tests show eventual recovery, not uninterrupted playback.
The 15-minute Windows TLS soak reported one 1.668-second freeze near 14m40s, with no OBS render/encoder skips. Its cause is unresolved; fresh repeats do not erase that observation.
TCP/TLS describes the browser-to-TURN leg. OBS still uses UDP; a UDP-blocked publisher was not tested.
Audio advancement and media clock arithmetic were checked; perceptual A/V synchronization was not measured.
This task changed the test harness and documentation, not OBS transport/encoder code, VDO.Ninja application code, or the production WHIP server.
